topics.SPA: Spatial: nets, cubes, mirrors and routes

questions.stem:
Leo says: 'Our class should have a fish tank. Looking after fish would teach us to be responsible.'
Which statement best supports Leo's argument?

options.A: Students would take turns to feed the fish and clean the tank each week.
options.B: Fish come in many bright colours.
options.C: The pet shop is close to the school.
options.D: Some students already have a dog at home.

questions.explanation: Leo's reason is that it would teach responsibility. Taking turns to feed the fish and clean the tank shows how the students would practise being responsible.

distractors.B: nice, but not about responsibility
distractors.C: about buying fish, not learning responsibility
distractors.D: not about the class fish tank

questions.stem:
Max says: 'It is raining, so the school cross-country race will be cancelled.'
What has Max assumed?

options.B: The race is always cancelled when it rains.
options.C: Max does not want to run.

questions.explanation: Max's conclusion only follows if rain causes the race to be cancelled. He hasn't said this; he has just assumed it.

distractors.A: the length isn't part of his reasoning
distractors.C: this might be true, but it isn't what his argument relies on

questions.stem:
A box of marbles is heavier than a box of shells. A box of shells is heavier than a box of feathers. A box of stones is heavier than a box of marbles.
Which box is the second heaviest?
questions.explanation: Put them in order: stones > marbles > shells > feathers. The second heaviest is marbles.

distractors.B: third heaviest

questions.stem:
Rule: To go on the class excursion, a student must bring a signed note AND a hat.
Ava: 'Tom brought a signed note, so he can go on the excursion.'
Noah: 'Pia went on the excursion, so she must have brought a hat.'
If the rule was followed, whose reasoning is correct?
questions.explanation: Noah ✓: everyone who went brought a note and a hat, so Pia brought a hat. Ava ✗: Tom also needs a hat, and we don't know if he brought one.

distractors.A: Ava forgets the hat
distractors.B: Tom may not have a hat

questions.stem: Olivia is 3 years older than her brother. The sum of their ages is 17. How old is Olivia?
questions.explanation: If her brother is 7, Olivia is 10, and 7 + 10 = 17 ✓.

distractors.A: that is her brother's age
distractors.B: subtracted 3 from 17
distractors.C: tried 11 + 6, which is 17, but 11 is 5 years older, not 3

questions.stem:
Sam's team wore their new green shirts and won the game. Sam says: 'We should always wear green shirts. They make us win.'
What is wrong with Sam's thinking?

options.A: Green is not a popular colour.
options.B: The team might have won for other reasons, like playing well or the other team being weaker.
options.C: The shirts might not fit everyone.

questions.explanation: One win while wearing green doesn't show the shirts caused the win. Lots of other things could explain it.

distractors.A: not the problem with the reasoning
distractors.D: good advice, but not the mistake in his reasoning

questions.stem:
Mum says: 'We should go to the beach on Saturday. It will be a sunny day.'
Which statement, if true, most weakens Mum's argument?

options.A: The beach is a 20-minute drive away.
options.C: The weather report says there will be strong winds and big waves on Saturday.
options.D: Everyone in the family likes swimming.

questions.explanation: Even if it is sunny, strong winds and big waves would make the beach unpleasant or unsafe, so it is a good reason not to go.

distractors.A: a short drive doesn't make it a bad idea
distractors.B: about last week, not this Saturday

questions.stem: These patterns are made from matchsticks. How many matchsticks are needed for pattern 20?
questions.explanation: Count: 7, 12, 17… Each new pattern adds 5 matchsticks. Pattern 20 = 7 + 19 × 5 = 102.

distractors.A: multiplied pattern 1 by 20: the shared sticks are counted twice
distractors.B: forgot the extra stick(s) at the start

questions.stem:
Some of the children at the party wore hats. All of the children who wore hats got a lolly bag.
Which statement must be true?

options.A: All of the children got a lolly bag.
options.B: No child without a hat got a lolly bag.
options.C: Some children got a lolly bag.
options.D: Every child who got a lolly bag wore a hat.

questions.explanation: Some children wore hats, and all of them got a lolly bag, so at least some children got one.

distractors.A: children without hats might not have
distractors.B: they might have got one too; we aren't told
distractors.D: the rule only goes one way

questions.skill: Who is where in a line
questions.stem:
Four children stand in a line for the canteen.
• Amy is somewhere in front of Ben.
• Dev is last in the line.
• Cass is standing right next to Dev.
Who is first in the line?
questions.explanation: Dev is 4th, and Cass is next to Dev, so Cass is 3rd. Amy is in front of Ben, so Amy is 1st and Ben is 2nd. Order: Amy, Ben, Cass, Dev.

distractors.A: check the clues in order
distractors.B: check the clues in order

questions.stem: Lucas's piano lesson starts at 4:15 pm and lasts 40 minutes. It takes him 25 minutes to walk home afterwards. What time does he get home?
questions.explanation: The lesson ends at 4:15 + 40 min = 4:55 pm. Walking home takes 25 minutes: 4:55 + 25 min = 5:20 pm.

distractors.A: that is when the lesson ends
distractors.B: added 15 instead of 25 minutes for the walk

questions.stem:
The school canteen usually sells about 50 pies on Fridays. Last Friday it sold only 10.
Which statement, if true, best explains this?

options.B: Pies cost the same as last year.
options.D: Last Friday, most of the school was away on an excursion.

questions.explanation: If most students were away, far fewer people were there to buy pies.

distractors.A: it always did, so this doesn't explain the change
distractors.B: nothing changed, so it doesn't explain it

questions.stem:
Ruby says: 'Our school's new reading program is working. More students borrowed library books this term than last term.'
Which statement, if true, most weakens Ruby's argument?

options.A: The library is open every lunchtime.
options.B: Ruby borrowed more books than anyone else.
options.C: Most students like reading adventure stories.
options.D: This term, every student had to borrow a book for a class project, whether they wanted to or not.

questions.explanation: If students HAD to borrow books for a project, that could explain the extra borrowing, not the reading program.

distractors.A: nothing has changed, so it can't explain more borrowing
distractors.B: about one student only
distractors.C: doesn't say why borrowing went up

questions.stem:
All of the birds Jo saw at the zoo could fly. So all birds can fly.
What is the mistake in this reasoning?

options.A: Jo should have gone to a different zoo.
options.B: Jo only saw some birds, so she can't be sure about all birds.
options.C: Some animals at the zoo are not birds.
options.D: Birds that can fly are faster than birds that can't.

questions.explanation: Jo saw only a few birds. You can't say something is true for every bird from a small group. (Emus and penguins can't fly!)

distractors.A: the problem is the reasoning, not which zoo

questions.stem:
Everyone in the school choir must go to practice on Wednesday. Ella is in the choir.
Ana: 'Ella goes to choir practice on Wednesday.'
Bo: 'Tim goes to choir practice on Wednesday, so he must be in the choir.'
If the information is true, whose reasoning is correct?
questions.explanation: Ana ✓: every choir member goes on Wednesday, and Ella is in the choir. Bo ✗: other children (like helpers or visitors) might go on Wednesday too; the rule only goes one way.

distractors.B: the rule doesn't say ONLY choir members go
distractors.C: Bo's conclusion doesn't have to be true

questions.stem:
If it is raining at lunchtime, the class eats lunch inside.
Cy: 'The class ate lunch inside today, so it must have been raining.'
Di: 'It wasn't raining today, so the class must have eaten outside.'
If the information is true, whose reasoning is correct?
questions.explanation: The rule only says what happens when it rains. The class might eat inside for another reason (too hot, or a special event). Cy ✗ and Di ✗.

distractors.A: they might eat inside for another reason
distractors.B: they might still eat inside when it's dry

questions.stem:
Zara has 9 coins. Some are 20-cent coins and the rest are 50-cent coins. Altogether she has $3.00.
How many 50-cent coins does she have?
questions.explanation: Try different numbers of 50c coins: 4 × 50c = $2.00, and the other 5 coins are 20c = $1.00. Total $3.00 ✓.

distractors.A: that is the number of 20-cent coins

questions.stem:
One of three friends ate the last biscuit. Only one of them is telling the truth.
Ash: 'Bree ate it.'
Bree: 'I didn't eat it.'
Carl: 'I didn't eat it.'
Who ate the biscuit?
questions.explanation: Try each person as the eater. If Ash ate it: Bree and Carl both tell the truth (two truths ✗). If Bree ate it: Ash and Carl tell the truth ✗. If Carl ate it: only Bree tells the truth ✓. So Carl ate it.

distractors.A: then two people would be telling the truth
distractors.B: then two people would be telling the truth
distractors.D: only one choice makes exactly one person truthful

questions.stem:
At a library, children can borrow up to 5 books. Children who return books late cannot borrow for a week.
Isla: 'Ben returned his books late yesterday, so he can't borrow any books today.'
Kai: 'Mia borrowed 5 books today, so she has never returned a book late.'
If the rules are followed, whose reasoning is correct?
questions.explanation: Isla ✓: returning late means no borrowing for a week, and today is within that week. Kai ✗: Mia may have returned books late long ago; the rule only stops borrowing for one week.

distractors.A: late returns only stop borrowing for a week
distractors.C: Mia could have been late more than a week ago

questions.stem:
There are 9 cupcakes, and all of them are shared out among 4 children (not always equally).
Eve: 'At least one child gets 3 or more cupcakes.'
Fin: 'At least one child gets 2 or fewer cupcakes.'
If the information is true, whose reasoning is correct?
questions.explanation: Eve ✓: if every child got 2 or fewer, that would be at most 8 cupcakes, but there are 9. Fin ✓: if every child got 3 or more, that would need at least 12 cupcakes.

distractors.A: Fin is right too: 4 × 3 = 12 is more than 9
distractors.C: Eve is right too: 4 × 2 = 8 is less than 9
distractors.D: test the biggest and smallest possible shares

questions.stem:
Only children who have finished their homework are allowed to play video games. Sam played video games today.
Gus: 'So Sam has finished his homework.'
Hana: 'Mia has finished her homework, so she played video games today.'
If the information is true, whose reasoning is correct?
questions.explanation: Gus ✓: only children who finished homework can play, and Sam played. Hana ✗: finishing homework means Mia is ALLOWED to play, not that she did.

distractors.B: allowed to play doesn't mean she did play

questions.stem: There are 24 students in a class. Every student has either 1 or 2 pencils, and there are 37 pencils altogether. How many students have 2 pencils?
questions.explanation: If every student had 1 pencil, there would be 24 pencils. The extra 37 − 24 = 13 pencils belong to students with 2. So 13 students have 2 pencils (and 11 have 1).

distractors.A: that is the number with 1 pencil
distractors.B: halved the class
